results.name: Gym Rowing Machine Sprint Speed
instructions: Sit on the rowing machine with your feet securely strapped into the footrests, knees bent, and hands grasping the handle with an overhand grip.
Push through your legs to extend your knees and drive your body backward, keeping your arms straight until your legs are almost fully extended.
Just before your legs are fully extended, pull the handle towards your lower chest by bending your elbows and squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Reverse the motion by extending your arms forward first, then bending your knees to return to the starting position. Repeat the motion at a sprint pace for the desired duration.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid rounding your spine throughout the exercise.
Use a moderate resistance level to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Exhale as you pull, and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Gym Rowing Machine Sprint Speed is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a rowing machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Lower Back, Shoulders, Arms.

results.name: Half Burpees
instructions: Begin in a high plank position with your hands placed directly under your shoulders and your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Quickly jump your feet forward towards your hands, landing with your heels on the floor in a squat position.
Immediately jump your feet back to return to the high plank position, keeping your body straight and your core engaged.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions, maintaining a quick and controlled pace.
tips: Focus on steady breathing, exhaling as you jump your feet forward and back, and inhaling as you hold the plank position.
Ensure your hands are placed directly under your shoulders in the plank position to maintain proper form and prevent strain.
Use a non-slip surface to prevent your feet or hands from slipping during the exercise.
results.description: Half Burpees is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a leverage machine, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Hand Stand Hold
instructions: Begin in a handstand with your hands shoulder width apart, your arms straight, and your legs extended overhead.
Press firmly through your palms and shoulders to keep your body lifted.
Engage your core and glutes while keeping your body as straight as possible.
Hold the position for the desired duration.
tips: Spread your fingers wide and press through your entire palms.
Keep your elbows straight without allowing your arms to bend.
Look toward the floor between your hands without lifting your head excessively.
Inhale and exhale steadily throughout the hold.
results.description: Hand Stand Hold is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core, Forearms.

results.name: Headstand
instructions: Place your forearms on the floor and clasp your hands behind your head, resting the crown of your head on the floor. Lift your hips and extend your legs together behind you.
Bend both knees and draw them toward your chest as you stack your hips above your shoulders.
Straighten both legs upward until your body forms a vertical line, then pause briefly.
Bend your knees, lower them toward your chest, and extend your legs behind you to return to the starting position.
tips: Press firmly through your forearms to reduce pressure on your head and neck.
Engage your core to control the raising and lowering phases.
Practise near a wall until you can maintain balance safely.
Exhale as you raise your legs and inhale as you lower them.
results.description: Headstand is an advanced multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the triceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Forearms, Hip Flexors.

results.name: Heavy Bag Sled Drag
instructions: Attach the sled to a rope or strap and hold it in both hands, or attach it to a harness.
Face away from the sled and lean slightly forward.
Walk or run forward with powerful strides, dragging the sled behind you.
Continue for the set distance.
tips: Keep your chest up and drive through your legs.
Keep tension on the rope; don't jerk it.
results.description: Heavy Bag Sled Drag is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a sled machine, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Forearms.

results.name: High Knees
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms at your sides.
Begin by lifting your right knee towards your chest as high as possible while simultaneously swinging your left arm forward.
Quickly switch to lift your left knee towards your chest while swinging your right arm forward, mimicking a running motion.
Continue to alternate knees rapidly, maintaining a steady rhythm and engaging your core. Repeat for the desired duration or number of repetitions.
tips: Lift your knees as high as possible while maintaining proper form and balance.
Move quickly but with control to maximize cardiovascular benefits and prevent injury.
Ensure your movements are balanced and coordinated to avoid straining your muscles.
results.description: High Knees is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves.

results.name: Indoor Cycling Spinbike Sprint
instructions: Set the saddle so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up at an easy pace.
Add moderate resistance and pedal as fast as you can for the sprint interval.
Recover at an easy cadence, then repeat the sprints.
tips: Stay seated with a stable upper body.
Keep enough resistance that you don't bounce in the saddle.
results.description: Indoor Cycling Spinbike Sprint is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Calves.

results.name: Indoor Cycling Spinbike
instructions: Set the saddle so your knee is slightly bent at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Hold the handlebars lightly and keep your back neutral.
Pedal at a steady cadence, adjusting the resistance to your target effort.
Keep a smooth, circular pedal stroke for the set time.
tips: Push down and pull up through the whole stroke.
Don't grip the handlebars too tightly.
results.description: Indoor Cycling Spinbike is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with a stationary bike, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Glutes, Calves.

results.name: Jogging
instructions: Stand with your feet hip-width apart and your arms relaxed by your sides. Engage your core and maintain an upright posture.
Begin jogging by taking short, quick steps, lifting your knees slightly higher than walking pace.
Swing your arms naturally with each step, keeping them bent at a 90-degree angle.
Maintain a steady, comfortable pace and continue jogging for the desired duration or distance.
tips: Gradually increase your jogging duration and intensity to build endurance and strength.
Breathe steadily and rhythmically to maintain oxygen flow during the jog.
Stay hydrated and take breaks if needed, especially during longer jogging sessions.
results.description: Jogging is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the cardiovascular system (cardio). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the cardio category. Secondary muscles: Glutes, Hip Flexors, Core.

results.name: Jump Rope Alternating Foot
instructions: Stand with your feet together, holding a jump rope with the handles in each hand. Position the rope behind you, ready to swing it over your head.
Swing the rope over your head and, as it passes under your feet, lift one foot off the floor, quickly followed by the other foot, allowing the rope to pass beneath both feet in succession.
Continue to alternate feet with each jump, lifting one foot after the other, maintaining a steady rhythm and keeping your jumps low and controlled.
Repeat the movement for the desired duration or number of repetitions, ensuring a smooth and continuous motion.
tips: Focus on quick, controlled movements, keeping your jumps low to minimize impact on your joints.
Use your wrists to swing the rope, rather than your arms, to maintain a smooth and efficient motion.
Wear supportive footwear to protect your feet and ankles during the exercise.
results.description: Jump Rope Alternating Foot is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the calves (lower legs). Performed with a rope, it falls under the plyometric category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings.
